title: The five oceans: how big is each one?

items.label: Arctic
items.ask: Why is the Arctic Ocean covered in ice?

explain.say: Here is a surprise: if you looked at Earth from space, you would see mostly blue. About 71 percent of our planet is covered by ocean. Look at the board. There are five oceans, drawn to size, and one of them is a true giant.

draw.text: The five oceans: how big is each one?

items.label: Arctic
items.ask: Why is the Arctic Ocean covered in ice?

explain.say: See the huge one? That is the Pacific Ocean, about 165 million square kilometres. It is bigger than all the land on Earth put together! It stretches from Japan and Australia across to Chile and California. Can you guess what Pacific means? Peaceful!

items.label: Arctic
items.ask: Why is the Arctic Ocean covered in ice?

explain.say: Next is the Atlantic, about 106 million square kilometres, between the Americas on one side and Europe and Africa on the other. Then comes the warm Indian Ocean, touching India, East Africa and Australia. Which ocean is closest to your home?

items.label: Arctic
items.ask: Why is the Arctic Ocean covered in ice?

explain.say: Now the Southern Ocean, the icy water that circles all the way round Antarctica. A strong current races round it without stopping. Can you see how much smaller it is than the Pacific?

items.label: Arctic
items.ask: Why is the Arctic Ocean covered in ice?

explain.say: The smallest is the Arctic Ocean, round the North Pole, covered in floating sea ice for much of the year. Well done, you know all five! Wow fact: the deepest spot in the Pacific, the Challenger Deep, is about 11 kilometres down, deeper than Everest is tall.

items.label: Arctic
items.ask: Why is the Arctic Ocean covered in ice?

faq.a: From biggest to smallest: the Pacific, the Atlantic, the Indian, the Southern and the Arctic Ocean. They are all joined, so really there is one world ocean with five names.
The Pacific Ocean, about 165 million square kilometres. It covers about a third of the Earth, more than all the land put together.
asks: How big is the Pacific Ocean?

faq.a: It is the cold ocean that circles Antarctica, held together by a strong current that flows all the way round. National Geographic began marking it on its maps as the fifth ocean in 2021.
asks: Is the Southern Ocean a real ocean?

faq.q: Why is the Arctic Ocean covered in ice?
faq.a: Near the North Pole the sun stays low, or does not rise at all in winter, so seawater freezes into floating sea ice. The North Pole is on this floating ice, not on land.
asks: Is the North Pole on land?

faq.a: On average the ocean is about 3,700 metres deep. The deepest place, the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific, is about 10,900 metres down.
asks: What is the deepest place on Earth?

facts: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by ocean.
The Pacific Ocean covers more area than all the land on Earth combined.
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 10,900 m deep.

quiz.why: The Pacific is the biggest, bigger than all the land on Earth together.

wrong.1: The Atlantic is the second biggest.
wrong.2: The Arctic is the smallest ocean.

quiz.show: The ocean that circles Antarctica is…
quiz.why: The Southern Ocean flows all the way round Antarctica.

wrong.1: The Indian Ocean lies between Africa, Asia and Australia.
wrong.2: The Arctic Ocean is at the other end of the world, round the North Pole.
